| [CLAIM-283](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-283.md) v3 | The precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it are different quantities: a motive can claim control without receiving it, and be granted control it does not claim | A4 §2, reading Frijda through the record: "control precedence also suggests a useful addition to our parameterization", a priority p_i claimed by a process, which "is not the same as granted influence I_i. An operator can urgently demand control without receiving it. That distinction between *claimed precedence* and *endorsed authority* may be essential to modeling internal conflict." It joins [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md) to the grant scheme. It does not say which wins. | Active |

| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) v5 | A grant scheme that denies each operator control over its own authority can make delegation do work: rewarded for how far their preferred policies are realized and not for authority held, operators delegate to aligned others, and the two conditions need not be confined to one-hop allocation | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-286](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-286.md) v4 | Habit, akrasia, rumination, rigidity and insight can be modelled as regimes of one organization, in which processes transform shared meaning and allocate one another's influence, with trust, specialization and higher-level agency arising from its history and not imposed | A7's central thesis, the explanatory half of the manuscript, kept apart from the constitutive half ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)) as A7 itself asked. | [CLAIM-287](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) v6 | What persists when a self persists through inactivity is the capacity to reinstate an organization, not its continuous running, and continuity of that kind can branch and merge, so it is not an identity relation | A6 §7 and A10 §4.3. | [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v7 | In a population whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed, the norms the organization appears to maintain are set by the modeller, not by the organization: they can become its goals through their role in selecting what persists, but it does not produce or revise them | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. A2 gives each operator an objective J_i, its evaluation of the collective decision, and A7 and A10 propose sufficiency tests run on such populations. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. | [CLAIM-296](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-296.md) v3 | What a system has, what it knows it has, and what it can deploy within a task's deadline are different, and the last is a relation among the resource, the agent, its environment, the task, the deadline and the cue, not a property of any one of them | A18's first candidate, from the owner's EMT case ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)): the drug was stocked, the EMT knew it, and it could not be found before the medic moved on. | [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md) v7 | When an operator's authority is updated by how well it performs on the interpretation it helped make dominant, the coupled meaning and influence of an organization can amplify an initial interpretive advantage without any gain in fidelity to independent evidence | A22's narrow claim and A23 VIII.E's central hypothesis, from the owner's U22: connect retrieval-mediated anchoring to the record's distributed agent as dual meaning and influence canvases ([CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md), [TERM-053](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-053.md)). | [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) | Under a deadline, search can establish presence by finding one item but absence only by exhausting the collection, so "If I can't find it, it isn't there" acts on an unfinished search as negation as failure acts on a finished one: a default stronger than either the closed-world assumption or negation as failure, safe only when the arrangement makes the full search finish within the deadline | The medic's "If I can't find it, it isn't there" ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)) and the owner's "if I can't find it quickly enough, it may as well not be there" ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) act on a failed search as if it showed absence. One find shows presence, but absence needs a check of everything, which a deadline forbids. First filed as negation as failure on a time bound, with Reiter and Clark unread. Both readings corrected it. The two assumptions are separate. Reiter's closed-world assumption is that the database is complete about the world. Clark's negation as failure is licensed only by finite failure: "the exhaustive but unsuccessful search for a proof". A search cut off by a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It assumes a closed world and that the unsearched part would have failed. It is safe when the full pass finishes in time. In [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the EMT knew the drug was stocked, which is exactly where Reiter shows the closed-world assumption inconsistent. So there it was a decision to stop, not an inference. | Superseded — by [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) |
| [CLAIM-307](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-307.md) v2 | Retrieval pressure and evidence are different criteria for carving a category, and they move in opposite directions with copy count: evidence that a distinction exists grows with its copies, the search a bin saves shrinks with them, so the bins a deadline forces are often the ones the data least supports | From [MOM-CLM-166](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-166.md), which reads the owner's LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) against a formalism that cited it with the sign reversed. [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md) says when a distinction is real enough to name. Its evidence grows with the number of copies. The parable says when a distinction must be built to act in time: a single brick among similar ones. Expected search falls as copies grow. The two answer different questions, "is it there?" and "can it be reached in time?", and come apart in both directions. MOM's table was re-run here and reproduced, and a simulation of the search agrees. | Active |
| [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) v2 | Sorting schemes over objects with determinate properties never conflict as descriptions, since the product of any sortings refines them all; they conflict as arrangements, since a fixed number of bins realizes one partition when each item is stored once, and which costs least depends on what is searched for and on what stands out within a bin | What is directionally right in the owner's LEGO monograph, as Mathematics of Meaning graded it. Its contextuality claim is empty: any sortings of bricks share a joint refinement ([MOM-CLM-137](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/claims.d/CLM-137.md)), and the events they generate stay Boolean ([MOM-ARG-047](https://github.com/dmarx/mathematics-of-meaning/blob/main/record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md)). Its intuition that builders cannot share a sorting is true of arrangements. One set of bins realizes one partition, the product may need more bins than there are, and the cheapest choice depends on what each builder searches for and on what stands out within a bin ([CASE-095](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-095.md)). The disagreement is a trade, not a failure of global truth. Sorting on one attribute also turns a search for a combination of features into a search for one feature within each bin, which Treisman and Gelade (LIT-1082, read) show is the difference between a serial scan and one found at a glance. | Active |
| [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) | A search cut off before an exhaustive pass can establish absence when the arrangement certifies that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item: a sorted table answers non-membership in a logarithmic number of probes, and the Threshold Algorithm stops early with its answer proved, so absence needs a certificate about the remainder, not exhaustion; similarity search in high dimension is where no such certificate exists | Filed at the owner's request, from the database readings set against [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry: presence by one find, absence "only by exhausting the collection". Sorted order and the Threshold Algorithm each establish absence from part of the collection, because the arrangement bounds what the rest can hold. Where the arrangement gives no bound, as in similarity search in high dimension, [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s asymmetry stands. | Active |
| [CLAIM-312](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-312.md) v3 | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" asserts operational unavailability, that the item will not be put to use before the deadline, not absence: a search that fails by the deadline establishes unavailability outright, and licenses absence only with a certificate that the unsearched remainder cannot hold the item, from exhaustion, from an invariant of the arrangement, or from a closed-world default | Restates [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) at the owner's request, after [CLAIM-311](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-311.md) showed that absence can be established without exhausting a collection. The owner's own wording in [CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md), "it may as well not be there", is hyperbole for operational availability ([TERM-055](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-055.md)), not a claim about inventory. Read so, the rule reports an outcome and needs no default. [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s analysis survives as the account of the literal reading: what a failed search must be joined with before it licenses absence. The gap between the two readings is [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md)'s Bayes term, and it matters when the statement is passed to someone who will act on presence. | Active |
| [CLAIM-313](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-313.md) v2 | A fixed number of bins realizes one partition only when each item is stored once: with copies, overlapping partitions coexist, as hashing-based similarity search stores each item in many partitions and pays for it in space, so sortings conflict as arrangements only under a one-copy constraint, which binds bricks but not index entries | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on locality-sensitive hashing (Indyk and Motwani 1998; Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten 2017) set against [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md)'s premise that "a set of k bins realizes one partition of the collection at a time". That holds when each item is in one place. An index can hold many copies, and hashing-based similarity indexes do exactly that, trading the space of the copies against query time on an exact curve. It narrows [CLAIM-310](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-310.md) to collections whose items cannot be copied, which includes the LEGO case; it does not touch the claim about descriptions. | Active |

It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) v3 | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). | [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) v3 | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
| [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md) v11 | A level of organization has a temporal facet as well as a compositional one: higher-level variables are characteristically slower and longer-lived than the activity that produces them, though slowness is a mark of a level and not its definition | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: "'higher level' doesn't just mean in terms of abstractions over abstractions, we should also expect 'higher level' effects to be on slower timescales than 'lower level' effects." The claim does not say that a slow variable is thereby a level, a system or an individual. | Active |

Promoted from a section of [QUESTION-119](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-119.md) at the owner's word, with A7's defeater priced by [CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md), which A7 said it needed. It does not say the fandom was the efficacious unit. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v11 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The mapping is the assistant's, A6, filed at the owner's request ("address the still open stuff"). At U8 the owner endorsed it as filed ("Yes, as filed"). It reads both lines into [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s operator model. The sharp edge: it says the lines share one model, not that either line's results transfer to the other unchanged. Each mapping is a hypothesis until a result on one line is shown to hold, through it, on the other. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-078](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md)) as SYNTHESIS-011, and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084); the thesis is the owner's and the mapping the assistant's, as filed. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) v2 | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. Sandved-Smith et al. cast mental action as policy selection over higher-level cognitive states; Brouillet and Friston make felt fluency an inference about the precision of one's own processing; Smith et al. let a generative model grow its own structure by inference and learning alone. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. A redescription with no action on the world concedes that action on the world is not part of the loop. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v5 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. The sharp edge: the mapping relocates sampling from the world to retrieval, which is [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md)'s move reversed, and it holds only if the agent's own store can surprise it as the world can. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-339](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-339.md) v3 | A judgement–observation loop cut off from action loses one route for evidence it did not select, and the free-energy principle's reason for minimizing surprise, that a persisting system must keep its states in bounds, needs action on the world, though a loop can confirm itself with action available too | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, narrowed at A4. Friston et al. (2010) say active sampling is "mandated by ergodic arguments based on the very existence of adaptive agents", and the enactive account puts a system's own norms in its capacity to act against tendencies toward its viability boundary. Kübler and Birbaumer's extinction hypothesis is the empirical form. As first filed it said a loop without action has a self-confirming minimum. [NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md) shows the minimum arises with action available, so the counter now claims only that losing action removes one source of evidence the loop did not select. [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) answers it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md) v2 | Scoring operators on predictions committed before the evidence is not by itself Regime B: in the linearized operator model the coupling of interpretation to conferral has the sign of κ′ − κ̄, so commitment removes capture only when the interpretation bends the reading of the evidence no more than it bends the predictions, and it keeps the learning that revising after the evidence would lose | The formal question [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) asked, answered in [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s linearization ([CASE-106](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-106.md)): is committing predictions before the evidence equivalent to Regime B? No. The coupling γ is 4ηs(κ′ − κ̄), where κ̄ is how far the shared meaning bends the committed predictions and κ′ how far it bends the reading of the evidence. It is corrective, null or capturing as κ′ is below, at or above κ̄. Strong correction can fail by oscillation when \|βγ\| ≥ 1 − αδ. Revising predictions after the evidence sets γ = 0 but also stops authority from tracking who predicts well. Linear, at the symmetric state, for squared-error scoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-341](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-341.md) v5 | The loop that keeps a lucid agent's model in touch with what it models runs between judgement and observation: each judgement reshapes the observer whose later observations it then judges, and action on the world is not part of that loop, so active inference's action–perception cycle misplaces where the agent is active | The owner's, U1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: Friston's free-energy approach is "generally correct, but the cybernetic model is wrong"; action can be cut out of the loop, which decomposes into "Judgement (qua measurement that generates interpretations) <--> Observation". At U2 the owner held that the pragmatic-transport and will-organization models are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". The claim is stated in that model's terms, as [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and in the diachronic form A4 proposed and the owner asked to be filed at U5 ("make the revisions"): a judgement need not produce the observation it judges, but it reshapes the observer that produces the next one. The sharp edge: the synchronic form, in which each judgement produces its own outcome, is not claimed. That is the open route of [TERM-039](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-039.md) and [CLAIM-127](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-127.md), and the record demoted it once before ([CLAIM-109](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-109.md)). | Active |
| [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) v9 | What keeps a judgement–observation loop from confirming itself is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests; action is one source of such evidence, not a necessary one, and a loop that selects its own evidence can lock in with action available | The assistant's synthesis, A3 and A4 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, filed at the owner's request at U5. Three results the record already holds. [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md): capture in the operator model needs both arrows of [CLAIM-297](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-297.md)'s circuit, and scoring operators independently of the dominant interpretation removes it. [CLAIM-141](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-141.md): a loop always has a distributional fixed point, so what binds it is a constraint that prescribes marginals. [THEORY-285](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-285.md) ([NOTE-766](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-766.md)): an active-inference agent locks in with action available, because its own sampling policy withholds the evidence that would correct it. The claim does not say action is unimportant, only that it is not what does the anchoring. | Active |
| [CLAIM-344](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-344.md) v5 | Resolve is a maintained organization of precedence, commitment and revision that keeps a temporally extended policy effective across changes in locally dominant evaluations while keeping the capacity to revise it; mere slowness or persistence is not resolve | The owner's frame, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "I think emergence of "resolve" could be an interesting frame within which to examine our will-organization framework." A37 defined it, and A39 to A47 revised it each turn: retention and revision as separate grades, fragility against rigidity (A41), access against authority (A42), and governance that makes its own repeated exercise unnecessary (A45, A47). The record already holds a theory of resolve, Ainslie's recursive staking of future choices ([THEORY-067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-067.md)); this is its organizational and revisable form, placed in [CLAIM-159](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-159.md)'s will-organization cell. The sharp edge: the standard for when revision is warranted is not supplied, and is [QUESTION-087](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md)'s open problem. | Active |
| [CLAIM-346](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md) v2 | Feasibility, aggregation and epistemic coordination are independent obstructions to an organization's realizing its demands: each can occur with the other two absent | Owner-seeded, U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: Arrow's theorem, then cryptography and "the two generals problem". Three elementary constructions, each with one obstruction and not the others, are given in the body. The sharp edge: the independence is relative to fixing the demands as the constituents' own acceptance conditions; that no remedy for one removes another is A36's further reading, argued in the body and not part of the claim. | Active |
| [CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md) v5 | Frustration among an organization's demands is an ordinal fact before it is a quantity: the jointly satisfiable sets of demands form a downward-closed complex whose minimal non-faces are the minimal conflicts, relief is strict enlargement of that complex for the same declared demands, reorganizations that relieve different conflicts are incomparable, and dropping or suppressing a demand is not relief | The owner's correction, U37 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "We can do quite a lot with access to an ordering, even if it doesn't give us a true measure." A37 granted it ("I agree with your correction") and built the acceptance sets, their intersection and the compatibility complex. Corrected here: acceptance conditions sit on attainable outcomes, a demand's form depends on whether it demands improvement or maintenance, and A37's weak-preference sets fail only as representations of improvement demands. The definitional facts are shown in the body, including that every pair of demands can be jointly improvable while the triple is not. The sharp edge: relief compares complexes for the same declared demands, so a reorganization that deletes a demand is not compared at all, and two reorganizations can be incomparable. It is the move [CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md) and [TERM-043](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-043.md) made for translation, in a new line. | Active |
| [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) v5 | No coarse-graining is normatively adequate in general because it preserves stability, prediction or aggregate performance: a description adequate for an institution's performance can merge states its members' claims must distinguish, so adequacy is fixed by the evaluative target, and the target cannot be justified solely by the description that preserves it | A21 §18's Candidate 2 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, with A21 §5's clause against circularity and A22's Construction C ([CASE-110](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md)). A21: "no coarse-graining may be treated as generally normatively adequate solely because it preserves organizational stability, predictive accuracy, or aggregate performance." The case is demonstrated: total output preserves an institution's every judgment and merges a member's claim. The general conclusion is interpretive. It is [CLAIM-152](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-152.md)'s target-relativity carried from individuation to evaluation, and [CLAIM-060](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-060.md) in the language of coarse-graining. Filed in distributed-agency because its case is a whole against its members. The sharp edge: it does not say which target is right, and it denies that the description can settle it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-351](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-351.md) v3 | A zero aggregate gradient does not show that the demands it aggregates are reconciled: with positive weights it holds both when every demand's own gradient vanishes and when nonzero gradients cancel, and in the second case no update improves them all to first order; even the first is only joint first-order stationarity, which a demand's maximum or saddle also has | A33 §5 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "Zero aggregate gradient does not imply absence of frustrated demands." With L₁ = (θ − 1)² and L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0 ([CASE-115](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-115.md)), the equal-weight gradient is zero and the aggregate is at its global minimum, while each loss is 1 and wants the opposite move. In general a vanishing positive combination of gradients is either every gradient zero or a certificate that no update improves them all, and the scalar cannot tell which. A29's "the unity of the distress signal need not arise from the unity of the underlying causes" is the interpretive reading, kept apart in the body. | Active |
| [CLAIM-353](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-353.md) v4 | A will-organization that gives two operators decisive jurisdiction over a pair of options each, respects unanimous preference and admits any profile of operator rankings cannot always choose, and unlike Arrow's impossibility this is not escaped by giving the grant procedure richer, cardinal or comparable, information, so what distributed governance must give up is jurisdiction, unanimity or the domain, not an informational restriction | From U36 of the exchange of 2026-10-17. [THEORY-027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md) says no in general, and its title holds the difference A36 cited without stating: "unlike Arrow's theorem, the conflict is not removed by interpersonal comparability". So A36's remedy, letting the grant procedure (TERM-101) use richer information, answers Arrow but not jurisdiction. The sharp edge: it holds only if operator jurisdiction is pairwise decisiveness, which [THEORY-027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-027.md) leaves open even for persons. | Active |
| [CLAIM-356](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-356.md) v6 | An objective that originates outside a learning system can become a goal of the training organization, through its causal role in selecting, stabilizing and reproducing the learned structure it rewards; exogenous origin does not disqualify a goal, but it does not show that the network governs or endorses the objective, and what is selected is performance on the updating distribution, not generalization | The owner's, U35 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, against A34's guardrail that "Loss minimization does not automatically mean the model has its own goals": the externally assigned objective "can motivate identification and persistence of learned features", so the training process can be described as "having endogenous goals". The sharp edge: the goal belongs to the training organization ([CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md)), not to the network, and nothing here says the network endorses or governs it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) v9 | The frustration residual and governance regret separate structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and identify none of them as thwarting: a positive residual says no admissible update meets every declared requirement, a positive regret only that the actual update's worst residual exceeds the best achievable, which can hold while every requirement is met, and actual violation needs regret above the negative residual; aggregate performance does not tell infeasibility from realized violation, and the multipliers that certify infeasibility need not be the weights governance assigns | A34 §4 and A35 §3.3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, restated at A39 §2C and A40 §3.4, from A33's "irreducible conflict" and "manufactured frustration". With m(d) the worst residual, Φ its minimum and Γ the actual update's excess over Φ ([CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md)): Φ > 0 is structural infeasibility; when Φ ≤ 0 the actual update violates a requirement exactly when Γ > −Φ. Positive governance regret establishes excess worst-case shortfall relative to the optimum, and can hold while every requirement is met. Neither quantity identifies an obstructing mechanism, a governance failure or active thwarting; governance-induced frustration needs an argument or intervention showing the allocation of influence responsible. A35: "Importantly, these dual multipliers are not endorsement weights." | Active |
| [CLAIM-359](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-359.md) v5 | A self-governing organization's robustness to compromised constituents is a property of the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, not only of its constraints on harmful acts; safeguards against capture can also restrict the disagreement and revision that self-governance needs, and where they do security and self-governance trade off, while others, such as audits independent of the audited that protect dissent, serve both, so the two are distinct achievements and not opposed ones | The owner's question, U41 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "is literature on organizational robustness to insider threats potentially useful to us?" A41's answer, condensed: an insider can aim at the organization's future allocation of authority rather than at the present decision, so robustness must protect the processes that allocate, audit and revise authority, and the same protection can silence the opposition that corrects the organization, though some safeguards protect both. | [CLAIM-361](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-361.md) v4 | Relief of an organization's frustration must be judged for an identified organization against a fixed reference set of its original demands, under an explicit correspondence between earlier and later demands: a demand excised or suppressed has changed the comparison and has not been satisfied, an endogenous revision of what the organization maintains is a transformation of it and not relief, and learning can change which processes bear the demands | The owner's prompt, U38 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, on A37's line that deleting a demand "has changed the comparison problem": "it might be helpful to connect back to our notions of individuation". The sharp edge: it does not say transformation is worse than relief, only that it answers a different question. | Active |
| [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | On a norm-ball update set the local frustration residual Φ_r = min over ‖d‖ ≤ r of max_i(ε_i + g_iᵀd) equals the maximum over the simplex of Σλ_iε_i − r‖Σλ_ig_i‖_*, so infeasibility of the declared improvements has a certificate, and any admissible actual update exceeds Φ_r by a nonnegative governance regret | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. | [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md) v6 | Whether a training-time regulatory condition belongs to a network depends on which unit is individuated for the training dynamics and whose jurisdiction governs the updates; in conventional training most of that governance falls to the optimizer–model–data system, so a condition of training is not thereby a condition of the network | The owner's correction, U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "it might help clarify things if we apply our individuation and volition frameworks to this system", the system being a deep network during training (U30). | [CLAIM-369](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-369.md) v5 | In symmetric resource-mediated competition with interaction matrix A = UᵀU and growth rates r = Uᵀb − c, Lotka–Volterra population dynamics are multiplicative gradient flow on the convex feature-selection objective ½‖b − Un‖² + cᵀn over the nonnegative orthant: the invasion fitness of an absent component is the negative partial derivative of that objective, and the uninvadable equilibria are its KKT points | From a synthesis the owner relayed on 2026-10-18 (workbench entry of that date), checked here and given a proof. | [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md) v4 | Under one-hop allocation within an epoch, an operator that grants influence to an ally whose policy is nearer its own than the collective decision is raises how far its preferred policy is realized while its own authority stays fixed, so the two conditions of the grant scheme hold together | The demonstrated core of [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md). | [CLAIM-386](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-386.md) v3 | For x(t+1) = (A* + εC)x with A* block-diagonal, the Simon–Ando aggregate Â = QAV has one-step closure defect exactly QA − ÂQ = QA(I − VQ); the part from the blocks' own dynamics vanishes iff every block has equal column sums, and then the whole defect is ε·QC(I − VQ) | Derived in the reading of Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Altenberg (2004), [NOTE-977](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-977.md), which states the Simon–Ando aggregate without an error term, and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-388](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-388.md) v5 | Exact dynamical closure of a collective variable does not require a nearly decomposable block: in a linear Gaussian VAR(1) with uniform coupling among n units, the sum of all units is exactly dynamically independent at every stable coupling strength, while every partition of the units into two or more groups couples as strongly across its edges as within them | From A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which gave the two-unit continuous-time case (ż = (b − a)z for z = x₁ + x₂) and the boxed slogan "Exact aggregation ⇏ near-decomposability". | [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) v2 | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), exact dynamical independence of a linear coarse-graining implies that its Mori–Zwanzig memory vanishes, but not conversely: memory needs coupling out of the coarse variable and back, and dependence needs only the way back, so a coarse variable can be Markov in its own law with zero memory and still be dynamically dependent | Derived in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-390](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-390.md) v2 | For a block of coordinates in a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), dynamical dependence is at most ½ log det(I + Σ_YY⁻¹ A_YR C A_YRᵀ), with A_YR the coupling into the block and C the covariance of the rest given the block's present state, so it is of second order in the coupling into the block, whatever the coupling out of it | First found in the reading of Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2000), [NOTE-989](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-989.md), as a by-product; derived and checked here. | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md)'s defeater counts a test-passing factor that is "by independent marks, not an agent". | [CLAIM-394](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-394.md) v2 | In a stationary linear Gaussian VAR(1) that is time-reversible (AΠ = ΠAᵀ, Π the stationary covariance), every slow-feature direction is a left eigenvector of A, so any span of slow features is an exactly dynamically independent coarse-graining; off reversibility a slow feature is in general neither independent nor free of memory | Derived in the reading of Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md), and re-checked here. It says when slowness, the criterion of slow feature analysis ([THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md)), picks out a closed coarse-graining in [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md)'s sense: always in the reversible linear Gaussian VAR(1), which is the class of noise-free square mixtures of independent AR(1) processes, and not in general otherwise. Linear features, linear Gaussian dynamics, lag one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) | Under Montévil and Mossio's definition of closure, a closed set of constraints has at least two members, and if each constraint is produced at the time scale of a constraint in the set that generates it and not at the scale at which it is itself conserved, the set includes at least one slow and one fast dependence, so a system with a single constraint of its own cannot realise closure |  | Active |

| [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md) v2 | For a scalar stationary process with autocovariance C, the Mori–Zwanzig memory kernels for the projection onto the current value are fixed by C alone, through C(m+1) = Σ_{k≤m} c_k C(m−k); the memory vanishes iff C is geometric, and when C has finite Hankel rank d the memory has Hankel rank exactly d − 1 | Derived in the reading of Lin and Lu (2019), [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1) on ℝⁿ, a scalar linear coarse variable Y = LX is, in its own law, an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1); so its Mori–Zwanzig memory, though non-zero at every lag in general, is carried exactly by finitely many coordinates that are functions of Y's own past and innovations | Derived in the reading of Chorin and Lu (2015), [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md), and re-checked here. | [CLAIM-400](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-400.md) v6 | In the meaning–authority model linearized at symmetry, a third, maintained legibility state that authority moves (ε) and that moves interpretation (ν) or conferral (μ), with persistence λ < 1 and nonnegative couplings, destabilizes the symmetric state exactly when the two-variable condition holds with β + νε/(1 − λ) in place of β and δ + με/(1 − λ) in place of δ: at the threshold the regime is indistinguishable from stronger two-variable couplings, and the slower it is the more it adds, while away from the threshold it adds a mode that no two-variable model has, so a lean in the regime can outlast the advantages it was built from | [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) asked whether authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence is a third channel with its own instability condition, or [CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)'s κ′ renamed. Both, in different respects. With a maintained legibility state r, det(I − J₃) = (1 − λ)[(1 − α)(1 − δ) − βγ] − ε[νγ + μ(1 − α)], which is (1 − λ) times [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)'s expression with β_eff = β + νε/(1 − λ) and δ_eff = δ + με/(1 − λ). | [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) v5 | The conditions an effective description is commonly asked to meet are not of one kind: predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection; so a matrix over them as independent binary axes conflates kinds | A4 and A5 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U4 ("it sounds like considering it from this angle has potentially already altered our characterization of those 'virtues'"). The record adds what A5 missed: memory is relative to the projection too ([QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), [CLAIM-397](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-397.md)), and THEORY-752's result holds only for the conditional-expectation projection. | [CLAIM-403](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) v7 | A contribution's admission to an organization's inquiry, its recognition in apt terms, its credibility, its uptake into judgements, and its contributor's part in revising the standards of uptake are separable, each possible without the later ones, so an organization can widen access while every channel by which a less authoritative contribution could change the criteria of authority stays closed | A24 §6 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U24: "Someone's contribution may be received and politely acknowledged yet have no mechanism through which it can change institutional understanding." It does not say that every contribution is owed uptake. | Active |
| [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) v14 | An organization can be governed from outside without any of its decisions being made for it, through the evidence its own procedures receive or through the criteria by which they weigh evidence; the two routes are distinct and each is possible without the other, so informational and evaluative independence do not imply each other; and where the organization's role is to evaluate another that affects its evidence or resources, the interpretation–authority loop can close between the two institutions, so that formal independence of the evaluator's procedure does not make its evaluation independent | The owner's cases, U20 ("maybe cases like reflexive control and regulatory capture could be informative here") and U21 (news-media capture) of the exchange of 2026-10-20, with A26 §4's two constructions and A27 §6. A26: "Neither guarantees the other." [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) holds the informational half and [CLAIM-348](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) the evaluative half. | [CLAIM-405](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-405.md) v2 | An individuation is well defined only once its criterion is fixed (the target it serves, the transformations its unity must survive, the scale), and that dependence does not make it arbitrary: once the criterion is fixed a verdict can be false, and differently fixed criteria can pick out units of one system whose boundaries cross rather than nest, none of them less real for it | The individuation counterpart of the owner's normative thesis [CLAIM-363](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md) ("once they are fixed, the judgment can be false"), as A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-20 put it, on the owner's U8 question about "contextuality/relativity/subjectivity". | [CLAIM-410](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md) v8 | Removing a constraint on an organization's members does not move it along one scale of more or less governance: it changes a profile of who holds governing positions, among them rule-making, monitoring, enforcement, appeal and revision, in which the authority the constraint held can be eliminated, distributed or transferred, and the members' first-order options and their share in revising the conditions of their action can move in opposite directions | The owner's question, U18 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what does this suggest about e.g. "deregulation" as an ideological end?" | [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v6 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". | [CLAIM-418](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-418.md) v5 | Possessing, enacting or being shaped by an organizational perspective does not establish an independent agent, and perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide: several agents can share a perspective, one agent can act through several, and a perspective can be reproduced with no agent governing it; where a perspective contributes to an agent's activity it can enable and constrain the exercise of agency, and that exercise can reproduce or transform it, while whether agency universally requires such a perspective stays open | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the owner's question at U38, "what's the relationship between perspective and agency?", A38's answer, and A39's request that it be recorded. | [CLAIM-421](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) v6 | The cessation of an organizational perspective's enactment need not imply the loss of the dispositions, capacities or reproductive relationships from which it can be reinstated: an interruption can be of activation (the disposition is held but not engaged or retrievable), of enactment (held, but the material, institutional or social conditions for exercising it are gone) or of reproduction (held by some bearers, but the processes that pass it on are damaged), and temporary unavailability is not extinction, though prolonged interruption of reproduction can end a tradition | From the branch of the exchange of 2026-10-22, at the owner's U37: the doorway effect as perspective meeting grounded experience, and the perspectival interruptions of the Chinese Cultural Revolution. | [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v6 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". | [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) v4 | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. | [CLAIM-451](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-451.md) v3 | When an organization's record of winning moves cycles, the failure is organizational nonintegrability, distinct from a perspective's own preference instability and from switching of the governing regime; it becomes organizational tension only when realized as costly reversal against demands the organization maintains, and cognitive dissonance only when that tension is detected and appraised as aversive; learning can relieve it by accommodation, by entrenched precedence or by cheap periodic coordination, which observed coherence does not tell apart, and ambivalence and nonintegrability entail neither one another | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A potential exists exactly when the finite relation of observed wins is acyclic": "rather than asserting potentials always have to exist, could we characterize cycles as a kind of internal tension or cognitive dissonance? preference/perspective/will instability?" | [CLAIM-452](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-452.md) v2 | For an organization whose response in each probe context is the authority-weighted mixture of its processes' known response profiles, the authority shares are identifiable from a set of contexts exactly when the processes' stacked profiles over those contexts are affinely independent; because the response is linear in the shares, local and global identifiability coincide, the condition is that the Fisher information of any design supported on those contexts is positive definite on the simplex's tangent space, and with binary outcomes at least one context fewer than there are processes is needed | When an organization's response in context c is p_π(·\|c) = Σᵢ πᵢ pᵢ(·\|c), the mixture [CLAIM-444](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-444.md) reduces the replicator model to, which probe contexts reveal its authority shares π? | [CLAIM-453](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-453.md) v2 | A population of perspectives, each advocating one of two interpretations, makes its collective choice by drift diffusion when the coordinate the decision is read from integrates independent evidence with no net leak or self-reinforcement and commitment is a bound on that coordinate; two interpretations make the reduction one-dimensional, but they do not by themselves give it | The owner's hypothesis at U34 of the exchange of 2026-10-24, continued: "if we've set up our simulation appropriately, when n=2 we should see drift diffusion dynamics".
