A34 qualified it, A35 gave the dial, and A36 gave an exact reduction for a network of accumulators. The record's own replicator construction gives a second, which the exchange did not see. Both were checked when filed. The sharp edge: two interpretations are necessary for a one-dimensional reduction, not sufficient. | Active |
| [CLAIM-454](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-454.md) v3 | A latent feature or mode recovered from an organization's members' activity is at most a constituent of an organizational perspective, not the perspective: a feature allocation says which members take part in which modes, and whether those modes are organized into one perspective depends on the relations of access, uptake and authority among their carriers, which the same allocation leaves open | From the Northstar turns of the exchange "Experimental Infrastructure Review", where the owner proposed inferring an organization's perspectives with hLDA (T21) and the Indian buffet process (T22). Every reply made the same reservation, and T22 put it most plainly: "None of those ingredients alone is the perspective. The organized relationship among them is." It is the criterion [QUESTION-276](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-276.md)'s answer has to meet. It does not say features are useless, or that no perspective is ever one feature's carriers. It says the allocation underdetermines the perspective. | Active |
| [CLAIM-455](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-455.md) v2 | For one bounded observer, a transformation of a representation can make one task's distinction legible and another's illegible at once, so legibility regimes are ordered only relative to a task, and a regime that improves one perspective's competence can disable another's | Stated in [CASE-154](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-154.md)'s title and its "What it can show" and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27 for propositions cases state that no claim holds. With two fair bits and an observer that reads one coordinate and cannot compute XOR, the raw pair gives 50% error on the XOR task and 0% on the first bit, and the XOR gives the reverse. [CLAIM-199](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md) says a garbling can raise usable information for a receiver; this adds that the same garbling lowers it for another task of the same receiver. The edge: one observer, two tasks; nothing about which task matters. | Active |
| [CLAIM-456](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-456.md) v2 | Maintaining a governing rule internally, by the organization's own reciprocal production, can be more fragile than having it reset from outside: arrangements identical in ordinary operation can differ in which losses are repairable, and the self-produced rule can be lost to a double loss or an interruption of the work that produces it which outside reset survives | Stated in [CASE-161](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-161.md)'s "What it can show" ("internal maintenance can be the more fragile arrangement") and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27. In the lab's 32-member population, with ordinary trajectories identical, reciprocal production restored one zeroed rule in 48 of 48 runs and both zeroed in 0 of 48, and lost both rules to an 80-update producer outage in 48 of 48, where external reset restored every case. An existence result in one stipulated population. The edge: it says nothing against self-governance, only that self-production is not robustness. | Active |
| [CLAIM-457](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) | That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable | A8 and A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, on the owner's CECOT case at U7: the United States said it could not bring a man back from Salvadoran custody, and El Salvador's president that he could not send him. Both can be true while the two together can, and the June 2025 return showed they could. Demonstrated by a construction. The edge: being able to realize an outcome together is not being responsible for it together, and feasible, authorized, willing and compellable coalitions are four families, not one. | Active |
| [CLAIM-462](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) v10 | An arrangement of institutions can keep, or increase, its capacity for effective action while its capacity to be effectively corrected by others degrades, because the two are maintained by different relations, so the first is no evidence of the second | A8's candidate central result and A9's conjecture, from the exchange of 2026-10-26: "A complex institutional system can preserve or even increase its capacity for effective action while losing its capacity for effective correction." It carries [CLAIM-422](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-422.md) (a correction is not a maintained capacity to correct) and [CLAIM-099](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-099.md) (effective action is not governance among regimes) from one organization to correction by other institutions. The edge: it is about relations, not about any government's conduct, and says nothing about which corrections are owed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-463](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-463.md) v2 | Restoring the conditions under which a capacity was lost need not restore the capacity: where the activity that maintains it reinforces itself, the same conditions can sustain both the capacity and its absence, so a capacity lost past a threshold returns only under conditions better than those it was lost under, or by rebuilding the activity directly, and restoring it can cost more than preserving it would have | A4's claim candidate from the exchange "About the Chagossians" of 2026-10-26, "Resource restoration does not imply organizational restoration", which the first filing declined because [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md) already derives it; the owner asked for it to be filed as a claim with its connection to the case. Demonstrated by [CASE-111](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-111.md)'s normal form: in the bistable range, returning the parameter to its pre-collapse value leaves maintenance at zero. The edge: a possibility shown in a model, not a finding about any grant program, people or institute, and a slow recovery is not evidence of the threshold. | Active |
| [CLAIM-464](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-464.md) v8 | An intervention can change what it would take to correct it: by altering the distribution of control, access, resources or enforcement before it is reviewed, it can make a specified corrective outcome costlier or unreachable while the standards that govern that outcome stay the same | A7 to A9 of the exchange of 2026-10-26, from the owner's U6 and U7: the police entry at USIP before any court ruled, the East Wing demolished before review, and transfers into foreign custody. A7 named it "endogenous remedial constraint", preferring that to fait accompli, which "describes an outcome but does not specify the causal mechanism". A possibility claim with three mechanisms: physical irreversibility, enforcement-mediated entrenchment and jurisdictional displacement. The edge: it says nothing about intent, and nothing about how much weight a court should give to risks the act created. | Active |
| [CLAIM-466](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-466.md) v3 | Lock-in from selectively admitted evidence and lock-in from self-scoring need different remedies: weighting admitted evidence by known, positive admission probabilities undoes the first and leaves the second, so correcting for how evidence was selected is not correcting how it is scored | Stated in [CASE-162](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md)'s "What it can show" and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27. In the lab's population, admission that depends on the record left the worse alternative in charge in 41 of 64 worlds, and exact inverse-propensity weighting brought that to 0 below full selectivity; with self-scoring alone (c = 0.5, nothing censored) 39 of 64 stayed wrong and the correction changed nothing. [CLAIM-404](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) holds that the informational and evaluative routes are distinct; this says their remedies are too. The edge: the correction is an oracle's, with known propensities. | Active |
| [CLAIM-467](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-467.md) v4 | Under full-information, independent audits, a learned allocation of influence among specialists is no better than a contextual router trained on the same audits, which is a mixture of experts whose experts earn responsibility by fitting better; whatever governance adds over routing has to be shown where evaluation fails, and the record has not yet found such a regime | The prediction [CASE-158](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md) states ("Under full information, governance should not beat it") and held by no claim, found in the audit of 2026-10-27; the runs were reported in [CASE-158](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-158.md) and reproduced in [CASE-162](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-162.md), where the router had the lower error in all four cells, selective and captured audits included. It gives [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md)'s objection a definite form for this model class. The edge: it bounds governance by routing under full information; it does not say governance never helps, and the regimes where it might ([QUESTION-271](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-271.md)'s four failures) are untested or, so far, lost. | Active |
| [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md) v5 | Physical interconnection can generate effective constraints on joint behaviour; measurement can estimate correspondences among local descriptions; and adaptive apparatuses can revise those correspondences; gluing expresses compatibility under specified relations, but neither the relations' physical generation nor their adequacy follows from gluing alone | The owner's U20 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, "interactions generate constraints that manifest as gluing conditions between intertial frames", restated at the owner's review. The readings found the correspondence maps given, measured or designed in nearly every formalism the exchange cited, and changed by interaction only in one constructed model whose authors call the result "learning to lie". So the claim separates three mechanisms. Physical interconnection changes what joint behaviour is admissible, and only it bears on the strong thesis that interaction generates constraints. Measurement estimates correspondences that already held. Adaptation revises an apparatus's own rules of comparison. The open question is [QUESTION-282](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-282.md): when interaction changes the physically operative correspondence structure, rather than revealing or redescribing it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md) | Coupling locally described systems necessarily induces a separation of time scales between their collective behaviour and their relative behaviour | The owner's, the second half of U20 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "coupling inertial frames necessarily induces scale separation (way less confident about this one than the former assertion)". Filed as said, with "inertial frames" read as the local descriptions of [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md). Rejected on filing: the necessity is refuted by conservatively coupled oscillators ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)), which A20, A21 and A23 all gave. The owner's doubt was well placed; what survives is a condition, and the condition is the interesting part. | Rejected |
| [CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) v7 | From interconnection to individuation, the relationships are distinct achievements that form a partial order, not a nested sequence: none implies the next, and a later one need not require every earlier one. Interconnection fixes what joint behaviour is possible, compatibility which local descriptions admit a coherent whole, dynamics which organizations persist, individuation which have sufficiently robust identity and boundaries, organizational autonomy which help maintain their own constitutive constraints, and inquiry which can measure and revise their own models and apparatuses under resource bounds, inquiry and reconstruction occurring without autonomy. The research program is to find the conditions for each, and their dependencies, apart from the order in which an inquiry meets them | Filed as CLAIM-474 at the owner's review of 2026-10-27, which asked for a synthesis "From Interconnection to Individuation: A Relational Constraint Research Program" that would make the theory "legible as a research program with distinct testable transitions, rather than a cluster of philosophically suggestive analogies". It references the record's claims rather than restating them: the places where one achievement does not yield the next, each with a source the record has read. Its premises, [CLAIM-471](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-471.md), [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md), [CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md), [CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md) and [CLAIM-475](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md), are Active. The central experiment is [CASE-179](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md). Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 as SYNTHESIS-006 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated, and returned to CLAIM under its own code on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084). | Active |
| [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md) v3 | Relata stand to relations as realizations stand to specifications: what an entity is, is partly fixed by the constraints on the configurations of entities and relations it can enter, and those constraints are themselves realized and maintained by something, so neither relata nor relations, nor specifications nor realizations, are prior without qualification | The owner's, U8 of the exchange of 2026-10-27, "maybe relata:relations::realization:specifications/constraints?", after U6 had set the record's ambitions as "extremely abstract and unrestricted". A8 sharpened it: "Relata are to relational structure somewhat as realizations are to specifications—but relations themselves also have realizations", and added the recursion, that constraints "are themselves realizations within larger relational structures". Filed unrestricted in domain, as the frame of which [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-136](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-136.md) are domain cases. It is not a structural realism that eliminates relata, and satisfying a specification is not being produced by it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) v6 | Rate differences help make structure and not only mark it: where some degrees of freedom settle faster than others by more than the rates vary among them, the relation they settle into is a constraint on the system over the window between the two rates, so what is a realization at one rate works as a constraint at another; and organization can make new rate differences in turn, as when modes slow near an instability and become order parameters, so hierarchies of rates and constraints can produce one another | The owner's, U12 of the exchange of 2026-10-27: "I think we may still have a coverage gap wrt scale separation and how that participates in creating structure". A12 agreed and found that the gap was synthesis, not literature: the record held [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md), [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md), [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md) and Mori–Zwanzig readings. It goes beyond [CLAIM-331](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-331.md), on which slowness is a mark of a level, in two ways: separation makes constraints, and constraints can make separation. It supplies the mechanism for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)'s recursion. It does not say that slowness is sufficient or necessary for a constraint, or that a constraint is an individual. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-480](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-480.md) v2 | Composing interactions can turn an interior into a constraint, and sometimes into a constraint of a new kind: in the chain E = ½k₁(x₁ − x₂)² + ½k₂(x₂ − x₃)², with x₂ internal and equilibrated, the boundary sees E_eff = ½·k₁k₂/(k₁ + k₂)·(x₁ − x₃)², a coupling between x₁ and x₃ that neither part has; if the interior relaxes slowly, eliminating it leaves a history-dependent constraint, a memory kernel, so interconnection fixes an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories and separation of time scales decides only whether that constraint is approximately memoryless; and for cellular sheaves the reduced constraint can relate three boundary values where every relation among the parts is pairwise | From A22 §4 and A23 §IV of the exchange of 2026-10-27, which called composition "the most important missing mechanism" after the owner's U20. Eliminating an equilibrated interior leaves an effective boundary relation that no part has; an outside system interacting only with the boundary meets it as a constraint, and "The interior has effectively become apparatus." Baez and Fong's black-boxing functor is the general theorem for passive linear networks. The memory case ties it to Mori–Zwanzig and to [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md): interconnection yields an effective constraint on the boundary's trajectories in every case, and separation of time scales decides only whether it is approximately memoryless. For cellular sheaves the reduction can need a richer relational vocabulary than the parts used (THEORY-1090; QUESTION-283). It is independent evidence for [CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md), that constraints are realized by organization. | Active |
| [CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md) v4 | Coupling does not by itself separate time scales: two identical undamped oscillators coupled with stiffness k have normal modes at ω₀ and √(ω₀² + 2k), nearly equal when k ≪ ω₀², and neither decays; separation comes where the coupling dissipates relative differences faster than collective ones, as in ẋ = −ax − k(x − y), ẏ = −ay − k(y − x), whose collective and relative modes relax at rates a and a + 2k, and in a Laplacian flow ẋ = −κLx, where the spectrum of L sets the rates | The answer A20, A21 and A23 gave to the owner's conjecture at U20 that coupling necessarily induces scale separation ([CLAIM-473](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-473.md)). Two small computations: conservative coupling splits modes without separating or damping them, and dissipative coupling damps the relative mode at a rate that grows with the coupling. For a Laplacian flow the kernel is exact compatibility and the nonzero spectrum is the hierarchy of relaxation rates, so a spectral gap is where the separation comes from. Conceded, so Active. It gives a mechanism for [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s second half and is not a test of individuality. | Active |
| [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. It is the record's answer to the question. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. The capacity to revise its governing standards when they break down does: the third capacity, which [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) names as taking part in governing the conditions of its own transformation. Two systems matched within a regime differ under it, and they diverge in behaviour once that regime breaks down. | Active |
| [CLAIM-490](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-490.md) | A fanbase is a mixture of spectators who relate to the club in different ways, as supporters, followers, fans and flâneurs, so the public stance credited to it is weighted towards the most committed types before any bias in who is sampled | From Giulianotti's taxonomy ([THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md)): supporters are hot and bound to the club as community, while flâneurs are cool consumers who switch clubs. The expressions that make up "the fans hate the owner" come from the hot types, and the cool ones take no part. So the stance is the committed segment's by composition, before amplification or preference falsification. It does not say the committed segment is a minority, or that its stance is illegitimate. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-491](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) v6 | No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity | The owner's position, from the discussion that raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). Selves come at more and less inclusive levels: social identity in self-categorization theory, fusion, self-expansion, interdependent self-construal. Apparent selflessness is then concern for a larger self. Cialdini et al.'s "oneness" result is its best evidence; Batson et al.'s rejoinder and the risk of trivial truth are its objections. It does not say people are self-centred, or that groups have no good of their own. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-492](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
| [CLAIM-493](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-493.md) v2 | When a fanbase is set against an outside party such as its club's owner, its more extreme members become more prototypical of it, so a vocal minority can fix the fanbase's public stance through a group process and not only through biased sampling of who speaks | A derivation from self-categorization theory: in an intergroup context the more extreme members of a group gain prototypicality (Turner et al. 1994, p. 458, reporting Haslam and Turner). If influence follows prototypicality (Turner 2005, unread), a fanbase opposed to its owner will treat its most hostile members as most representative. A minority stance can then become the fanbase's public stance by a group process that A2's preference falsification and amplification do not need. It does not say that the private majority agrees. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-494](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-494.md) v2 | Empathic concern for another produces motivation whose ultimate goal is the other's welfare, and it does so when perceived self–other merging is controlled, so not all helping is concern for an extended self | The empathy–altruism hypothesis as Batson et al. (1997) defend it against Cialdini et al. (1997): in experiments (two, by the SEP's account), empathy predicted helping with self–other merging controlled, and merging did not mediate it. Sober and Wilson (1998; [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)) argue on independent grounds that psychological egoism is not established. Filed as the empirical objection to the owner's thesis; both papers are unread, so the record holds the disagreement, not its resolution. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-495](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-495.md) | For an O(d)-valued connection on a connected graph, the assignments that meet every edge relation xᵢ = Tᵢⱼxⱼ form a space isomorphic to the vectors at one vertex fixed by every holonomy based there, which is the kernel of the connection Laplacian; for d = 1, and for U(1) phases, that space is all or nothing, but for d > 1 a connection whose loops are not trivial can still keep a subspace on which every loop is, so compatibility among local frames can be partial and graded by direction; and edge maps that do not commute can compose to a flat loop, so non-commutativity is not holonomy | From A2 and A3 of the exchange "Paper assessment" (2026-10-29), which drew it out of [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md)'s O(d) setting against [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md)'s U(1) one. The proof and the example are the record's, checked numerically. It is the zeroth cohomology of the connection sheaf, so standard, and it says nothing about which organizations have such transports. | Active |
| [CLAIM-497](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-497.md) v2 | A system's causes are found at the coarsest description whose interventions are unambiguous: a macro description is causally proportionate where it merges only micro states that intervention cannot tell apart, and no coarse-graining carries more causal information than the micro description it supervenes on | The record's position on causal emergence after [THEORY-787](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-787.md) was rejected. A coarse-graining can be the right causal description, but not by beating the micro. Under one intervention distribution at both levels, no coarse-graining of a transition carries more effective information than its micro ([THEORY-1167](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1167.md)). The ones that lose nothing are exactly causal feature learning's partitions, which merge only micro states with the same interventional effects ([THEORY-1169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1169.md)). The step from there to "the causes are found at the coarsest such description" is the record's own, in the sense of proportionality. It does not say the macro adds causal information. | Active |
| [CLAIM-500](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-500.md) v2 | The governance-induced kind of frustration is not idle: some failures of an organization's actual updates to meet demands that an admissible update would meet are explained by how influence is allocated, and not by step size, curvature, noise, conditioning or a fixed weighting rule | Split from [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) by the eighteenth status review ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [CLAIM-357](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-357.md) separates structural infeasibility, realized violation and minimax suboptimality, and says none of them identifies thwarting. This claim is the thesis that its old defeat condition tested: that the governance-induced kind does work an optimizer analysis does not, because some satisfiable demands go unmet through the allocation of influence. Untested; A39's case study 2 on [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md) would test it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-502](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-502.md) v2 | Multi-hop delegation can keep an operator's authority exactly independent of its own grants: under leave-one-out damped delegation, which counts the authority reaching each operator only along paths that have not already passed through it, an operator's grants raise the authority of every operator its grantee reaches and leave its own unchanged | A construction that shows [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md)'s old title false. Compute each operator's authority from A2's damped recursive rule with that operator's own outgoing grants removed. Then authority reaches it along paths of any length, but only along paths that have not passed through it, so nothing it grants can return to it. Its authority is exactly independent of its own grants, and a grant moves authority two hops and more. It does not say the rule conserves authority, that it closes the social route of moving others' grants, or that [CLAIM-375](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-375.md)'s guarantee carries over. | Active |
| [CLAIM-506](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-506.md) v2 | The split of the last eukaryotic common ancestor's central carbon metabolism, archaeal enzymes in the cytosol and alphaproteobacterial ones in the mitochondrion, does not single out syntrophy: a host that kept its own archaeal glycolysis and took up a bacterium with a TCA cycle leaves it whether the partnership began in syntrophy or by engulfment by an already complex host, and what the split counts against is a host whose carbon metabolism was replaced by the symbiont's | Split from [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1109.md) reports what Santana-Molina and colleagues find and that they read it as support for syntrophy; this claim is the record's judgement that the split cannot carry that reading. | Active |
| [CLAIM-508](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-508.md) v2 | Gene ancestries alone cannot tell a symbiotic partner from a source of transferred genes: a partner whose genes were mostly lost, replaced or spread thin would leave the diffuse trace that Tobiasson and colleagues read as piecemeal transfer, and Bernabeu and colleagues concede that their donor signals say nothing of the kind of interaction | Split from [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). [THEORY-1104](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1104.md) reports Tobiasson and colleagues' reading of diffuse bacterial genes as transfer; [THEORY-1105](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1105.md) reports Bernabeu and colleagues' concession about their own donors. This claim is what the record draws from both. | Active |
| [CLAIM-509](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-509.md) v2 | Stem lengths alone do not establish an order of acquisition in eukaryogenesis, neither Pittis and Gabaldón's late mitochondrion nor Bernabeu and colleagues' transfer waves: normalized stem length measures time only if rates before and after LECA are proportional, it shortens as closer relatives are sampled, the alphaproteobacterial separation from other bacteria rests on P = 0.044, and on Tobiasson and colleagues' data it does not behave as a clock | Split from [THEORY-1102](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1102.md) and [THEORY-1101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1101.md) by the twenty-second status review ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md)'s kind 2, the record's own extrapolation). The two readings, now Active, report what the papers find; this claim is the record's judgement of what stem lengths can establish. | Active |

Not claimed. A24's answer: "We have not established that corrigibility is unconditionally desirable." Filed because the owner asked, so it marks a real boundary. | [CLAIM-513](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-513.md) | Across a family of goals, a world model is not an optional explanation of competent behaviour: in a fully observed, finite, communicating, stationary environment, a goal-conditioned policy within a factor 1 − δ of optimal on every composite goal of depth n fixes every transition probability to within √(2P(1 − P)/((n − 1)(1 − δ))), so observers reading the same policy must ascribe the same world model; what it leaves open is whether a predictive component is realized inside the agent, since a lookup table over histories and goals has the same policy | From the reading of Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt ([LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md)), registered as the objection to watch against the owner's U20 thesis [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md). It defeats that thesis's functional reading only. The thesis's defeated_if is not met: the theorem holds "regardless of ... architecture", makes no matched-resource comparison and no intervention on internals, and its authors say the map runs "from the agent's policy rather than its activations". Within its scope, though, calling a world model an explanatory attribution is too weak. The bound was re-derived and checked against an adversarial agent. | Active |
| [CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). Both are kept, with each stated about a different notion of world model. Proposed: a definition and an organizing thesis, with the study [CASE-187](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) as its test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-515](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-515.md) v2 | Whether an organization has a cognitive property is four questions, not one: what information about the property can be recovered from its behaviour, what capabilities it can actually exercise, what mechanisms realize them, and whether it can maintain or transform those mechanisms; the four can come apart, and none should be silently substituted for another | The general principle the owner drew at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): "When asking whether an organization 'has' a cognitive property, distinguish the information recoverable from its behavior, the capabilities it can actually exercise, the mechanisms realizing those capabilities, and its ability to maintain or transform those mechanisms." It was drawn from the world-model case ([CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md)) and judged "sufficiently general—and sufficiently testable—that it deserves an explicit place in Nucleation's research program". Interpretive: its instances are demonstrated case by case, and the generalization is not. | Active |
| [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md) | Where every constraint capacity turns over at a positive rate and is produced only by others, with no basal production and production vanishing as its producers do, capacities whose production graph is acyclic all decay to zero: a capacity that persists needs a productive cycle among its ancestors, and removing a feedback edge set extinguishes every capacity; a cycle is necessary and not sufficient, and a one-member cycle is not closure | From A10 §1 and §5A of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), after the owner's "try to progress the theoretical program". The proof was rechecked by the reader of U7–U10. It is known in substance from autocatalytic-set theory, as A10 said. What it adds to the record is the boundary with closure: the necessary cycle may be a self-loop, and a self-loop is not closure in [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)'s sense or [CLAIM-395](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-395.md)'s, which need two or more constraints. | Active |
| [CLAIM-517](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-517.md) v2 | A successor regulator keeps a viable set positively invariant if, at every boundary context, its response distribution is within γ/L in total variation of a regulator that certifies inward margin γ, the dynamics being L-Lipschitz in that distribution; an average distillation loss certifies this only through coverage of the boundary contexts, so fidelity measured in ordinary operation certifies nothing about viability | From A16 §4 and §5 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), the owner having quoted its conclusion at U17: "preserving a regulator's response distribution sufficiently accurately can guarantee preservation of a physical organization's viability". The algebra was rechecked; the regularity conditions A16 left implicit are stated here. | [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". A20 agreed and gave the construction, with a limit the claim keeps: the attribution "sometimes ... names a genuine, interventionally identifiable computational mechanism". | [CLAIM-520](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md) v2 | The value of keeping a corrective capacity is conditional on objectives, uncertainty and cost: a free, optional audit cannot lower a single time-consistent decision-maker's expected performance, but an audit that costs C to maintain and bears on k decisions with error rate ε is worth k(0.25 − 0.5ε) − C in the exchange's model, negative when C is large or k small, and where no hypothesis fits the world, correction gains no reward and improves only calibration | From A24 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), answering the owner's U24 question whether corrigibility's desirability had been established. | [CLAIM-521](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) v3 | An organization's present coupling strength need not reveal the stability of the process maintaining it: in a constructed system whose maintained connector and capacities set a three-unit coupling, the recovery rate of the maintenance goes to zero at its saddle-node while the coupling's spectral gap there stays near 0.989 | From A12 §6 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31), which called it "a surprising result". All numbers were recomputed. | Active |
| [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) v6 | Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two | From A10 §4 (its Proposition 5) of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) v9 | For a normatively relevant discrepancy to change what an organization does, three distinct achievements are needed and any can fail while the others hold: legibility, by which the discrepancy becomes recognizable; volitional efficacy, by which a corresponding demand can move action; and correctability, by which a fitting revision can be carried out within deadline and resources; none establishes that the demand or the revision is justified, and whether the norm-satisfying histories the agent can still realize are empty depends partly on what its earlier actions destroyed | The owner's synthesis at review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md) v2 | Describing persons and organizations as coexisting levels of one process removes the question of how already-constituted agents add up to a collective, but not the question of levels: whether a collective variable has dynamics of its own, closed against the activity that realizes it, can be decided on a process description that presupposes no agents, is sometimes decided no, and a closed collective variable can be an aggregate that coexists with its realization while keeping none of its members' distinctions | Filed on reading Bencherki & Iliadis 2021 and Bencherki, Brummans & Vézy 2024, who hold that the "scaling up" problem "vanishes the moment communication is viewed eventfully" ([LIT-1902](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1902.md), p. 1364) because persons and organizations are "different informational levels that preserve all the characteristics of their organized components" ([LIT-1922](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md), ms. p. 21, proposition 2). The record's closure results show what survives. What vanishes is the picture of agents adding up. What remains is whether a higher variable runs on its own, which is a question about variables and is decidable. The record's own case of a closed collective variable is a sum, an aggregate, that coexists with its units, so "stages or coexisting levels" is not a dichotomy. It does not say that the agent picture is right, or that organizations are aggregates of members. | Active |
| [CLAIM-528](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-528.md) v2 | That a mechanism realizes a capacity can mean that the capacity is produced through it over time or that the capacity consists in it at a time, and interventions show only the first: a pathway whose disabling changes the capacity after a delay is a cause, can be intervened on surgically, and can be located relative to a declared boundary, whereas every intervention on a capacity that consists in its parts also changes some part along another path, so that relation is underdetermined by intervention data and is inferred by abduction or from simultaneity and settled parthood; and which of the two a given dependence is depends on the time resolution at which a description treats the parts' response as instantaneous | Filed on reading the fat-handedness debate after Craver: Baumgartner & Gebharter 2016, Baumgartner & Casini 2017 and Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel 2020. It does not say that constitution is unknowable, or that the record's organizations have constituents in the mechanists' sense. | Active |
| [CLAIM-529](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-529.md) v4 | An organization can be individuated without presupposing it as a declared candidate whose verdict can come out false: criteria stated on the candidate's interactions (whether benefit can be booked per member, which interactions the others depend on, what removing an interaction type does, whether its order survives release from an outside scaffold) apply to a grouping not yet assumed to be a unit, while criteria stated as members' attitudes toward the group (a goal about it, belonging, identity) make it partly constituted by being taken as one, individuating it by a different relation, unavailable where members have no such attitudes | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)). Criteria on members' attitudes toward the group (shared goal, belonging, focal goal of sustaining it) individuate constitutively, which is not the non-circular route and is unavailable for organisms without such attitudes. It does not say the paper argues this, and it leaves the presupposed lower-level units where the paper leaves them. | Active |
| [CLAIM-530](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md) v3 | Where maintenance is realized is a question of constitutive relevance only through its parthood condition: an internal producer and an outside controller supplying the same production law as state feedback meet mutual manipulability's two manipulability conditions identically, since disabling or stimulating either changes the maintained capacities and intervening on the capacities changes the activity of either, so what puts one inside and the other outside is parthood, a boundary the experiments presuppose and do not find | The record's join of [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) with the mechanist account of constitution, from Craver and Bechtel's admission that interlevel experiments are symmetrical and show componency only prima facie ([THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md)). In [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s pair the bottom-up and top-down interventions come out alike for producer and controller. So the criterion separates them only by its parthood clause, which is [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s declared boundary. The criterion is cited as Baumgartner and Gebharter state it (LIT-1934, p. 8, read in full in NOTE-1493); Craver's own texts stay unread. It does not say no criterion can draw the boundary. Closure, a producer that is itself maintained by what it produces, is a candidate that [CLAIM-522](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s one-variable model cannot express. | Active |
| [CLAIM-531](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-531.md) v4 | Generative entrenchment does not by itself give organizational closure: an entrenched core, which later interactions depend on so that perturbing it is catastrophic and perturbing them tolerable, can sit at the root of an acyclic dependency order, and where interactions turn over such an order persists only while something outside supplies its core; an organization that is both entrenched and closed has a core containing a cycle of mutual maintenance, each interaction on which is itself core unless its share of the maintenance is redundant | Filed on re-reading Griesemer & Shavit 2023 ([LIT-188](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-188.md), [NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)), who mark the step from conexus to community by generative entrenchment of core interactions and then, with "Hence", by organizational closure. Entrenchment as they define it is a one-way dependency order, and a tree rooted in its core passes their knockout test; closure needs the core to depend in turn on the set. By [CLAIM-516](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-516.md), read for interactions, an acyclic order persists only on outside supply, which is their own scaffolded conexus. It does not say their communities lack closure, only that entrenchment and knockout do not show it; and it reads Wimsatt's concept only as they quote it. | Active |
| [CLAIM-532](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) v6 | An unresolved discrepancy is an occasion for self-formation, the transformation dimension of a will-organization, and not a guarantee of it; it suffices for self-formation that the agent's own activity on such a discrepancy produce a maintained capacity, either a new distinction, its policy coming to depend on a feature of its situation it did not depend on, or a new channel, the outcomes it can reach under its own policy growing, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones, as shown by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone and by interventions on the processes that produce the capacity while it forms | The positive account A33 §7 offered, at the owner's U33 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), sharpened by the reader of U32–U33 so that it can fail. A33 wrote it; adopting it is the owner's call. It is a non-libertarian reading of Kane's self-forming actions ([CLAIM-022](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-022.md)'s note of 2026-11-02). The steps A33 chains, discrepancy to discrimination to response to maintained capacity to revised governance, are not a sequence ([CLAIM-474](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md)). | [CLAIM-535](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) v5 | An organization that acts on what it observes has a policy acceptable in every circumstance exactly when, for each observation, the circumstances it cannot tell apart share an acceptable action; so every circumstance having an acceptable action does not give a policy, a finer observation never removes one, and where acceptable actions overlap the coarsest observations that suffice are several and incomparable, so which distinctions must be made legible depends on which acceptable action the organization commits to | A33 §4 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's U33 request for positive accounts, with A30 §2's example and A32's Claim B. What it adds to [CLAIM-350](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md), its single-valued case, is found by the reader of U32–U33: with overlapping acceptable sets, legibility is relative to policy. A positive characterization of what legibility must supply for action. | Active |
| [CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md) v3 | A categorical model of perspectives and an LDA-style model differ in where the mixture lives: the first draws every act's perspective from one fixed categorical distribution, the second gives each episode its own mixture, drawn from a Dirichlet, and draws each act from it; the Dirichlet is a distribution over mixtures, not the perspectives themselves, and with symmetric concentration a over K perspectives two acts in one episode share a perspective with probability (a + 1)/(Ka + 1) against 1/K across episodes, so the concentration runs from one perspective per episode, as in persona selection (a → 0), to a fresh independent draw for every act (a → ∞) | The owner's U12 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), stated precisely: "H1 isn't LDA like though. that's my point. it's a categorical distribution. the topics in H@ are the dirichlet distribution which parameterizes the categorical distribution, which is what distinguishes H2 from H1 and why H2 is an LDA." The structure is right; one word is not. The Dirichlet is a distribution over each episode's mixture, and the topics, here the perspectives, are the categories that mixture weights. The agreement formula, derived here and checked by simulation, shows that both readings of H1 are limits of H2. | Active |
| [CLAIM-537](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md) v2 | In tolerance-bounded compatibility on a graph with disturbed offsets, \|Dx − a₀ − w\| ≤ δ for \|w_e\| ≤ η_e, a compatible configuration exists for every disturbance exactly when \|cᵀa₀\| + Σ η_e\|c_e\| ≤ Σ δ_e\|c_e\| on every cycle, and one configuration serves every disturbance exactly when η ≤ δ and \|cᵀa₀\| ≤ Σ(δ_e − η_e)\|c_e\|; an agent that chooses its configuration from what it observes needs the second condition within each class of disturbances it cannot tell apart, so whether a compatible state can be selected lies between the two and depends on what the agent can read | A30 §§2–3 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), at the owner's "keep going", with the second and third conditions derived by the reader of U30–U31 and checked by simulation (500 random instances, no mismatch). | [CLAIM-538](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) | On a finite graph of contexts whose overlaps carry preferred real offsets a and tolerances δ_e ≥ 0, an assignment within every tolerance, \|Dx − a\| ≤ δ, exists exactly when no cycle's holonomy exceeds the sum of its tolerances; with every δ_e > 0 the least uniform enlargement of the tolerances that admits one is the largest ratio, over simple cycles, of holonomy to summed tolerance, so the obstruction is certified by a cycle; the feasible allocations of tolerance depend on the offsets only through their class in H¹, so local adjustment can move a mismatch among the overlaps of a cycle and never remove it; and an evaluation that omits one overlap of every witnessing cycle reports a compatibility that does not hold | The owner's U27 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), "compatibility of tolerance bounds", with U28's pointer to the record's sheaf tools, worked out at A28 §3 and A29 §§3–4, 7 and A32's Claim A. The feasibility criterion is the classical feasible-differential theorem of network flows (Rockafellar 1984; no checked identifier, not registered), and the ratio is LP duality, so the result is granted, not the record's discovery. What the record adds is the reading: the frontier is an invariant of the obstruction class, governance chooses where on it the mismatch falls, and omission can fake compatibility. Checked by linear programming against brute-force cycle enumeration on random graphs. | Active |
| [CLAIM-543](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-543.md) v5 | What separates a language model's distribution over personas from a distribution over organizational perspectives is not whether the latent model is hierarchical, since a mixture or an LDA-style admixture already is, but whether some latent components condition which others are available or consequential: a model whose components are exchangeable given their weights is organizationally flat however many levels its prior has, and dependencies among components count as organization (organization as relational arrangement) only where interventions, not fit, support them | The owner's U8 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02): "think of the relations as bayesian hierarchy, so H1 is a flat plate model and H2 has hierarchical/causal structure", said of a language model read as a distribution over perspectives under the Persona Selection Model (U6). The precise form of the owner's H1/H2 contrast is [CLAIM-536](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-536.md). Interpretive: the contrast is argued, and no study yet separates the two kinds of model on a language model. | Active |
| [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) v4 | If a willed agent is the jurisdiction of its will-organization, then governing one's own governability is in part governing one's own individuation, in the constitutive sense of individuation at that level: a revision of the will-organization that changes which regimes it governs changes which willed agent there is, so a self-forming revision can be a re-individuation and not only a change in an agent's states, and whether the revised jurisdiction continues the earlier agent is a question of continuation, not of resemblance | The join the owner's U31 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02) asked for, "connect to individuation", made through the owner's own entry for it, [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md), which A31 never cited. A positive account, filed under U33. The reader of U30–U31 drafted it; adopting it is the owner's call. It names its sense of individuation, as [TERM-088](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md) asks and A31 did not: the constitutive sense, relative to [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md)'s level and target. [CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md) is its nearest held neighbour, a self as an organization that takes part in governing its own transformation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-546](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md) v4 | Negative frequency dependence that keeps two types in coexistence does not make their interaction cooperative: in Hawk–Dove with cost C above value V each type increases when rare and they coexist at the interior equilibrium of V/C Hawks, with Hawks still taking the whole resource from Doves, and on the Black Queen account producers of a leaked good and the cells that use it without paying coexist at a frequency set by the community's need; so whether types persist together and whether they cooperate are separate questions, and a coexistence criterion answers only the first | From §3 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04: "stable coexistence of strategies is not necessarily the same as stable cooperation: cooperators and defectors can coexist without eliminating exploitation". The record held the ecological half, invasion growth when rare ([CASE-118](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-118.md)), and a case of the point (the Black Queen, [THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)). It did not hold the point itself. Hawk–Dove makes it exact. The wording is the reader's; the twenty-fifth status review adopted it on 2026-11-06. | Active |
| [CLAIM-547](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md) v3 | Cooperation within groups and the coexistence of groups are distinct targets that can trade off: in the group-selection rule of Nowak's five, b/c > 1 + n/m, cooperation spreads because a group that grows to size n splits and another group is driven extinct, so the mechanism that stabilizes cooperation inside groups works by removing groups; cooperation local to a group, the persistence of several groups whose interests are opposed, and concern for those outside one's group are three achievements, and none of them secures the next | From §7 of the synthesis "The Evolution of Cooperation: From Coexistence to Symbiosis to Morality", which the owner supplied on 2026-11-04. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. | [CLAIM-690](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) v3 | Whichever way a whole and its part depend on each other, the same magnitude of dependence can run either way, and what sorts it is who controls the terms on which it is met, exit, renegotiation and the conditions of supply, while the magnitude and the integration that produced it set only how much rides on it: with the part able to withdraw or renegotiate, the whole's need of it becomes the part's hold on its terms; with the terms at an agent's discretion, the same need gives the part none, and the part's own dependence becomes vulnerability to that agent, on whom, under a principle grounding obligations in such vulnerability, the strengthened responsibility falls | The assistant's, offered at step 12 of the filing of "About Plantation Paradise" ([#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488)) and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13. | [CLAIM-1046](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1046.md) v2 | The observational partitions a family of affordable probes induces are not the lattice of possible decompositions: the map from probe subsets to partitions sends a union of families to the common refinement of their partitions, but an intersection of families to a partition that can be strictly coarser than the finest common coarsening, so its image is closed under meets and not under joins, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members against the Bell number of partitions of the configurations | A15 §2 says "the lattice of all partitions of Ω is generally much larger than the set of partitions realizable by our affordable probes", and that the probe lattice "is a structure of which distinctions our methods support", not of selves. For fixed configurations Ω and fixed response laws, let π(Q) be the partition of Ω into classes no probe in Q separates. Then π(Q1 ∪ Q2) is the meet (common refinement) of π(Q1) and π(Q2), while π(Q1 ∩ Q2) is at least as coarse as their join and can be strictly coarser. So π is order-reversing and meet-preserving, its image is a meet-closed part of the partition lattice and need not be a sublattice, and with m probes it has at most 2^m members, against Bell(\|Ω\|) partitions (32 against 115,975 for m = 5 and \|Ω\| = 10). | [CLAIM-1182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1182.md) | A comparison of genetically related with unrelated parent–child pairs, as in donor-gamete and adoption designs, can attribute an effect to what the gamete carries but cannot by itself divide it between DNA and a germline epigenetic mark, since both travel with the same parent; dividing them needs one person's gametes formed before and after the exposure | The donor-gamete design (Rice et al., [THEORY-2297](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2297.md); Lewis et al., [THEORY-2280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2280.md)) is the one human design that removes both the womb and rearing from a comparison of what a child inherits. | [CLAIM-1183](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1183.md) v3 | In a simulated sensor network whose correspondences drift, revision improves prediction on positions the network did not choose only when it answers to beacons whose position and channel the revision can neither rewrite nor refuse; revision by the sensors' disagreement alone restores consistency and not accuracy, and a revisable beacon map or a right to refuse disagreeing beacons loses part or all of the gain | From [LEAD-177](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-177.md)'s top rung ([CASE-390](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-390.md)): four sensors, drifting maps, 40 seeds. | [CLAIM-1186](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1186.md) v2 | A response profile that is positive, linear and normalized in the continuous test is a probability measure, and a declared family of tests turns the largest disagreement between two such measures into a pseudometric, which is a metric exactly when the family separates measures, so that observational equivalence under the family is distance zero | A26 of the exchange "Explain First Contact RL" (2026-11-22), answering the owner's U13 and U14 ([CLAIM-1112](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1112.md)). On a compact Hausdorff space X, the Riesz–Markov theorem represents each positive, normalized linear functional on C(X) by a unique regular Borel probability measure. For a declared family F of tests, d_F(μ, ν) = sup over F of \|∫f dμ − ∫f dν\| is a pseudometric, a metric when F separates measures (1-Lipschitz tests give Wasserstein-1; the unit ball of a characteristic kernel's space gives MMD). Fills by the assistant: linearity in the test is the premise that does the work, F must be uniformly bounded (or the measures share moments) for d_F to be finite, and a measure is not a metric. | [CLAIM-1194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1194.md) v3 | Where no process holds evidence on a block of tasks that does not come from the proposals themselves, a governance rule that treats its members alike cannot tell honest dissent from an attack that pushes the same block as hard: in a world and in its relabelling, with the dissenters' and attackers' targets swapped, it ends in the same place, so what it gains for the dissenters in one world it gains for the attacker in the other | From [CASE-415](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-415.md)'s relabelling check.
